key_insight: Random projections let multi-copy quantum measurements be performed on a smaller Hilbert space, trading coherent hardware complexity for more state copies and sampling.
engineering_relevance: This gives hardware-constrained quantum platforms a tunable way to estimate nonlinear quantities like tr(ρ^K) without requiring full-scale swap-test-style coherence.
method: Project each n-qubit state onto a q-qubit random subspace before the collective measurement.
Perform the multi-copy observable estimation on the reduced space.
Use Haar-averaged formulas to recover projected moments and quantify copy overhead.
evidence_signal: The abstract provides explicit scaling laws, including an estimated copy cost of O(2^((n-q)(K-1))) for tr(ρ^K) after compression.
watch_item: The approach lowers coherence demands, but the sampling overhead grows exponentially with the number of projected-out qubits and with K.
paper_title: Random Projections for Multi-Copy Quantum Algorithms
